annotations.text:
What actually makes the reference bar good

1. It is an OBJECT, not an edge. Floating, inset from all three edges, with a hairline border and its own shadow — so content scrolls under it and it reads as a control surface rather than the bottom of the page.

2. A LUMINANCE LADDER. Three steps: page, then the bar (lighter, translucent), then the active item (lighter again). This is the part your read didn't name, and it is what lets the active state work without colour.

3. The active state is a FILLED SHAPE hugging its own item — it does not stretch, and the label goes from grey to white at the SAME weight. Shape and lightness, never hue.

4. HEAVY ICONS. Filled or ~3px strokes, large against a small label. Ours are 1.8px outlines; these are 2.2px, which is as far as our line set goes before it muddies.

5. RED APPEARS EXACTLY ONCE, as a state dot on one icon. That discipline is what buys the colour-free active state — the same trade §2.2 makes.

Option A — Ladder

The reference logic in our neutrals: page #08080A, bar rgba(22,22,26,.78), active rgba(255,255,255,.10). Three steps of light, no hue anywhere in the bar except the waiting count.

For: the most faithful adaptation, and the quietest — it never competes with the hero card above it.

Against: the least assertive of the three. At a glance in sunlight the active item is a subtle step, not an announcement.

Option B — Bone

The active item is a solid bone capsule (#EDE4DC) with near-black icon and label — the same move as the Send button and the high-value chip. §2.2 already names bone as the queue's brand carrier.

For: unmissable, and it ties the bar to the one colour the queue is allowed to use for brand.

Against: it is the loudest thing on the screen. On the queue that is a problem — the breach card should win, and here the nav argues with it.

Option C — Well

Inverts the ladder: the BAR is the lit surface (rgba(255,255,255,.075)) and the active item is carved into it — a near-black well with an inset shadow.

For: distinctive, and physically legible — pressed rather than raised. Idle items sit at #A8A29C rather than #6E6863, so the whole bar is more readable.

Against: a lighter bar over a near-black page draws more attention to the chrome than any of them, and inset shadows are the first thing to look cheap if the blur is off.

What the bar obscures

All three float 20px above the bottom edge with a 14px side inset, so the list genuinely runs underneath — the fourth row is half-covered here on purpose, because that is what scrolling looks like.

In the app the reserve grows to match: .main's bottom padding becomes bar height + inset + safe-area, so the LAST row always clears it. probe:layout already asserts every tap target stays 44px, so a bar that ate a row would fail rather than ship.

The safe-area inset stays on the bar's bottom offset, not its padding — a floating bar needs the home indicator BELOW it, not inside it.
